Lithium-sulfur batteries suffer from rapid capacity fade associated with polysulfide dissolution and migration.
The polysulfide shuttles lithium ions through the separator during cycling, which the operando measurements directly resolved.
This shuttling mechanism leads to self-discharge and anode corrosion in practical cells.
Operando X-ray fluorescence mapping confirmed the spatial distribution of sulfur species across the cell stack.
Modified separators with ionic sieving layers were investigated as a mitigation strategy.
